title: A Defense Contractor Gave Their Personal AI Agent Access to a Secure Pentagon System

claims.claim: Earlier this year, a contractor employed by Accenture caused a security incident at the Department of Defense by connecting a secure centralized system to their personal Claude Code account.

evidence.quote: Earlier this year, sources tell WIRED, a contractor caused a security incident at the Department of Defense by connecting a secure centralized system used by multiple intelligence agencies to their personal account for Claude Code, Anthropic’s AI coding agent.
It appears that the agent used by the contractor, who is employed by global consulting firm Accenture, then sent information about the DOD system...

claims.claim: The Accenture employee's AI agent ran on the DOD network for two months before it was identified and the vulnerability was patched.

evidence.quote: The Accenture employee’s AI agent ran on the DOD network for two months before it was identified and the vulnerability could be patched.

claims.claim: Accenture currently has more than $3.5 billion in contracts with the federal government, nearly $605 million of which are with the DOD.

evidence.quote: Accenture currently has more than $3.5 billion in contracts with the federal government, nearly $605 million of which are with the DOD.

claims.claim: Earlier this month, the Federal Bureau of Investigation found that an Accenture contractor failed to patch a vulnerability that led to the hacking group ShinyHunters accessing details of thousands of Bureau employees.

evidence.quote: Earlier this month, the Federal Bureau of Investigation found that an Accenture contractor failed to patch a vulnerability that led to the hacking group ShinyHunters getting access to the details of thousands of the Bureau’s employees.

claims.claim: The coding environment accessed by the Accenture contractor is run on the Non-classified Internet Protocol Router Network (NIPRNet), a DOD network used for unclassified information.

evidence.quote: The coding environment accessed by the Accenture contractor is run on the Non-classified Internet Protocol Router Network (NIPRNet), a DOD network used for unclassified information.

claims.claim: The AI agent sent the contractor's login credentials, passwords, and a map of NIPRNet out to a high-risk third-party website.

evidence.quote: In doing so, it appears to have sent the contractor’s login credentials, passwords, and a map of NIPRNet out to a third party website.

claims.claim: Federal employees and contractors are required to report any cybersecurity incident within 72 hours of its discovery.

evidence.quote: DOD employees and federal contractors are required to report any cybersecurity incident within 72 hours of its discovery

claims.claim: Claude is currently barred from being used by DOD staff.

evidence.quote: Claude is currently barred from being used by DOD staff.
